review_notes: I read the whole file. I checked the likely competitors in Mathlib: `Mathlib/RingTheory` (spectrum topologies and Nullstellensatz) and a Mathlib-wide search for Zariski topologies and instances. I also listed the definitions in the sibling file QuotientClosedPoints.lean. Mathlib has no Zariski or other topology on coordinate tuples `σ → K`. It only has `PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology` and `MaximalSpectrum.zariskiTopology`, and the latter is also an induced topology. I did not check Mathlib's scheme-level affine space `𝔸(n; S)` against `ZariskiSpace`, so a competing version there is not ruled out. The wrapper structure `ZariskiSpace` carries the topology induced by `pointToPoint`, so it is not a second version of `PrimeSpectrum` or `MaximalSpectrum`. It exists to avoid putting a conflicting topology on `σ → K`, which the file states as its intent. `coordinatesEquiv` and `zeroLocusEquiv` are thin bridges between the wrapper and Mathlib's types. `zeroLocusClosedPoint` and `zeroLocusEquivClosedPoints` wrap the repository's own QuotientClosedPoints definitions, so they are not duplicates of Mathlib. The file also defines `zeroLocus` and `basicOpen` on the wrapper. These are named specialisations that reuse `MvPolynomial.zeroLocus` and `aeval`, and I found no practical cost to consolidating them. The case for consolidation is unclear, so I abstain.
